title: Conformal Counterfactual Inference under Hidden Confounding

problem.claim: Causal decision making needs predictions of potential outcomes and uncertainty intervals for counterfactual outcomes, including under hidden confounding.

gap.claim: Existing counterfactual interval methods either assume strong ignorability, which excludes hidden confounding, or require unidentifiable bounds relating observational and interventional distributions.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes wTCP-DR, a transductive weighted conformal prediction approach for counterfactual confidence intervals under hidden confounding.
The paper proposes wSCP-DR, a two-stage split-conformal variant of wTCP-DR intended to reduce computational cost while retaining the stated marginal coverage guarantees.
The paper derives conditions under which the proposed algorithm is strictly advantageous relative to a naive method using only interventional data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe wTCP-DR as a novel approach and wSCP-DR as a proposed two-stage variant.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed approach is reported to provide marginal coverage guarantees for counterfactual outcomes under hidden confounding.
The authors report that wSCP-DR has the same marginal coverage guarantees as wTCP-DR at significantly lower computational cost.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world data, including recommendation systems, are reported to show superiority over state-of-the-art baselines in coverage and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Potential-outcome uncertainty intervals are presented as useful for reliable personalized decision making.
Counterfactual prediction with uncertainty is identified as a fundamental causal-inference challenge, with existing methods limited by strong ignorability or unidentifiable bounds.
The paper introduces wTCP-DR, using a fraction of randomized-trial data to address covariate shift under hidden confounding.
The paper states theoretical advantage conditions and introduces wSCP-DR to reduce the computational cost of transductive conformal prediction.
The intervals are extended to individual treatment effects, followed by synthetic and real-world evaluations against baselines.

source_observation.claim: A fraction of randomized-trial data is used to account for covariate shift between observational and interventional distributions.

interpretation.claim: Combining observational data with limited interventional data may relax assumptions needed for uncertainty quantification under hidden confounding.

application.claim: When randomized data are limited but available, use it to calibrate or adjust observational counterfactual interval procedures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the required fraction of interventional data or the precise assumptions under which the approach applies.

source_observation.claim: The split-conformal variant is presented as substantially less computationally costly than the transductive method while preserving the stated marginal coverage guarantees.

interpretation.claim: Replacing a costly transductive procedure with a split procedure can improve practical scalability when the claimed coverage property is maintained.

application.claim: Prefer the two-stage split variant when computational cost is a deployment constraint.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the computational savings or characterize cases where the split variant may be less effective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact assumptions, coverage definition, or finite-sample conditions.
The abstract does not provide dataset sizes, numerical results, or baseline details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility beyond reporting code availability.
